title: Évariste Galois — Mathematical Works (1897): Modern English Reader with Editorial Notes / Œuvres mathématiques (1897) : lecteur anglais moderne avec notes éditoriales
description:
Open the complete linked English reader or download it directly.

This edition translates the complete substantive content of Évariste Galois's Œuvres mathématiques (Paris: Gauthier-Villars et fils, 1897), covering physical source pages PDF001–PDF096 / W01–W11. It includes the front matter, Émile Picard's Introduction, every collected work and fragment, historical notes, formulas, contents, and colophon; figures and blank-page topology are accounted for. The historical text is translated faithfully. Adjacent human-readable editorial notes explain corrections, mathematical qualifications, counterexamples, and witness differences without silently altering the source. Full proof, propagation, search, and provenance evidence accompanies the release.

The completed 21-task research program records 10 repaired results, 9 proved results, and 2 rejected claims, with no unresolved task. Three preliminary-image questions remain open outside that task set because the available images do not support a secure reading. The evidence includes 36 source-error records, 48 dependency edges, 52 prior-notice records, 22 documented searches, and a 242/242 cold audit.

Historical author: Évariste Galois. Edition identity and maintenance: Manuscript Typesetting Project. Post-P13 web research and mathematical certificates were supplied by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol in Pro mode. The modern-English translation, critical integration, DOI release engineering, and independent QA were supplied by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol in Ultra mode. No human translator is asserted.

Stable English concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21924301. Exact English release DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21926209. French source-language concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21923856. Global project: 10.5281/zenodo.20393488. Repository: github.com/KokunoYumeto/evariste-galois-en.

DataCite intent: the English concept IsTranslationOf the French concept, and the French concept HasTranslation the English concept. Because Zenodo does not currently expose those relation values, this record uses isDerivedFrom the French concept as the machine-readable fallback; the exact directions are preserved in the README and evidence sidecar. The separate isPartOf relation identifies the global project only.

The 1897 historical work is public-domain source material. CC0 1.0 applies to project-owned translation, editorial apparatus, typesetting, metadata, scripts, and evidence only to the extent the Manuscript Typesetting Project owns the relevant rights. Third-party scans, catalogue metadata, and witness artifacts are not relicensed. Release closure uses source replay, model/agent checks, deterministic builds, rendered inspection, hashes, and honest unresolved disclosure; no human-review gate is imposed.
